12	
13	**[1. Introduction and Background]{.underline}**
14	
15	Our firm represents the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the \"Committee\") appointed on March 28, 2025, by the United States Trustee in the Chapter 11 case of Meridian Consumer Products, Inc. (\"Meridian\" or the \"Debtor\"), Case No. 25-10347-KWH, pending before the Honorable Karen W. Hensley in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, 824 N. Market Street, Wilmington, DE 19801.
16	
17	Meridian is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 4200 Southpark Drive, Suite 800, Charlotte, NC 28217. The Debtor manufactures and distributes mid-market household cleaning products and personal care items. Meridian filed its voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code on March 14, 2025.
18	
19	The filing was precipitated by the loss of the Debtor\'s largest retail account, BrightMart Stores, Inc., in the third quarter of 2024, compounded by a product recall in October 2024. For fiscal year 2024, Meridian reported pre-petition revenue of approximately \$285.3 million and negative EBITDA of approximately \$8.7 million. The Debtor\'s funded debt totals approximately \$142 million, consisting of a \$95 million first lien credit facility with Ridgeline Capital Partners, LLC as administrative agent and \$47 million in 9.5% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2027 issued through Cornerstone Trust Company as indenture trustee. Trade payables at the time of filing were approximately \$67.3 million. Total assets are approximately \$156 million against total liabilities of approximately \$221 million, resulting in negative equity of approximately \$65 million. Cash on hand at petition was \$4.1 million.
20	
21	The Debtor is represented by Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP as bankruptcy counsel. The Debtor retained Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC as its financial advisor under an engagement letter dated January 8, 2025. The Committee has retained Pinehurst Capital Advisors LLC as its financial advisor.
22	
23	**[2. The Preference Exposure Report]{.underline}**
24	
25	Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC, through its Managing Director Jonathan Gao, prepared a Preference Exposure Report dated April 30, 2025 (the \"Report\"). The Report was provided to the Committee on or about May 1, 2025 pursuant to an informal discovery request.
26	
27	The Report identifies approximately \$18,732,614 in aggregate potential avoidable transfers under 11 U.S.C. § 547, covering 237 individual transfers to 84 unique payees during the 90-day preference period (December 14, 2024 through March 14, 2025). The Report includes narrative sections --- Executive Summary, Methodology, Analysis of Transfers, Defense Assessment, Statute of Limitations, and Recommendations --- as well as the following supporting exhibits: Exhibit A (Summary by Payee), Exhibit B (Tier Classification), Exhibit C (Detailed Transfer Schedule), Exhibit D (Contemporaneous Exchange Detail), and Exhibit E (New Value Calculation for Vanderhoff Chemical Supply Co.). The Report references but does not attach Exhibit F (Payroll and Insider Compensation Records) and Exhibit G (Wire Transfer Records for Consolidated Plastics International, Ltd.).
28	
29	The Report categorizes transfers into three tiers: Tier 1 (greater than \$500,000), Tier 2 (\$100,000 to \$500,000), and Tier 3 (less than \$100,000). The largest payees identified include Vanderhoff Chemical Supply Co. (\$6,800,000), Lakeshore Packaging Solutions, LLC (\$3,100,000), TerraFreight Logistics, Inc. (\$2,900,000), Sagebrush Marketing Group, LLC (\$1,800,000), Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc. (\$1,500,000), Consolidated Plastics International, Ltd. (\$1,400,000), and DataStream Enterprise Solutions, Inc. (\$1,200,000).
30	
31	Of note, BrightMart Stores, Inc. is identified both as a former customer --- whose account loss precipitated the filing --- and as a creditor owed approximately \$4.2 million for returned product credits and co-op advertising obligations.
32	
33	**[3. Scope of Assignment]{.underline}**
34	
35	Daniel, you are assigned as the senior associate responsible for conducting a comprehensive review of the Report and all supporting documents. The scope of your review includes the following categories:
36	
37	> **(a) Arithmetic and Reconciliation Review.** Verify all transfer totals, tier subtotals, payee counts, and the grand total by cross-referencing summary figures against the underlying transfer detail in the exhibits. Confirm that Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 classifications are consistent with the stated thresholds (\$500,000 and \$100,000). Recompute any aggregation or netting calculations.
38	>
39	> **(b) Entity and Classification Accuracy.** Verify that each payee is correctly identified, properly classified by tier, and that the correct legal entity is named as the transferee. Pay particular attention to any payees involving foreign parent entities or domestic subsidiaries and confirm the actual recipient of funds per bank and wire records.
40	>
41	> **(c) Legal Analysis of Defenses.** Evaluate the Report\'s analysis of each preference defense asserted under § 547(c), including:
42	>
43	> \(i\) *Ordinary course of business defense (§ 547(c)(2))* --- assess whether both the debtor-creditor prong and the industry-standard prong have been properly analyzed under the current post-BAPCPA disjunctive standard;
44	>
45	> \(ii\) *Contemporaneous exchange for new value (§ 547(c)(1))* --- verify that all transfers claimed as substantially contemporaneous actually meet that standard based on the timing reflected in the transfer detail;
46	>
47	> \(iii\) *New value / subsequent advance defense (§ 547(c)(4))* --- verify the chronological sequencing of transfers and new value, ensuring new value is not double-counted or credited against the wrong transfer; and
48	>
49	> \(iv\) *Any other defenses asserted*, including earmarking doctrine claims --- assess proper application of the doctrine.
50	>
51	> **(d) Insider Transfer Analysis.** Review payroll and insider compensation records (Exhibit F) and any other available data to determine whether the Report adequately identifies and analyzes transfers to insiders (as defined in 11 U.S.C. § 101(31)) during the one-year look-back period (March 14, 2024 through March 14, 2025). Note that insiders include officers, directors, persons in control, and their relatives. Specifically review payments to Gerald R. Hutchins (former CEO, resigned June 30, 2024), Rebecca Liu-Whitford (current CFO), and Marcus Thibodeau (VP of Sales, reported to be a relative of Mr. Hutchins).
52	>
53	> **(e) Foreign Transferee and Enforceability Issues.** Assess whether the Report addresses practical enforceability challenges for any preference judgments against foreign entities, particularly Consolidated Plastics International, Ltd. (Hong Kong). Cross-reference wire transfer records (Exhibit G) to confirm the identity of the actual transferee.
54	>
55	> **(f) Trust and Fiduciary Payment Analysis.** Evaluate whether any transfers identified as preferences may involve funds held in trust or fiduciary capacity by the payee (e.g., insurance premium pass-throughs). Review the Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc. broker services agreement to determine whether premium payments were held in a segregated trust account. Assess whether such payments constitute \"an interest of the debtor in property\" under § 547(b)(1).
56	>
57	> **(g) Statute of Limitations Verification.** Confirm the Report\'s stated deadline for commencing preference actions under 11 U.S.C. § 546(a)(1). The petition date and order for relief is March 14, 2025.
58	>
59	> **(h) De Minimis / Small Transfer Safe Harbor.** Verify that the Report applies the correct threshold under § 547(c)(9) as currently in effect for cases filed on or after April 1, 2022.
60	>
61	> **(i) Hypothetical Liquidation Analysis.** Assess whether the Report\'s assumption regarding the hypothetical Chapter 7 distribution to unsecured creditors (for the § 547(b)(5) \"improvement in position\" element) is supported by an attached or referenced liquidation analysis.
62	
63	**[4. Documents for Review]{.underline}**
64	
65	The following documents are being provided to you in connection with this assignment:
66	
67	1\. **Preference Exposure Report**, dated April 30, 2025, prepared by Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC (file: preference-exposure-report.docx) --- including Exhibits A through E as contained therein.
68	
69	2\. **Payroll and Insider Compensation Records** (file: payroll-insider-records.xlsx) --- referenced as Exhibit F in the Report but not attached thereto; obtained separately from the Debtor.
70	
71	3\. **Wire Transfer Records --- Consolidated Plastics International, Ltd. payments** (file: wire-transfer-records-cpi.xlsx) --- referenced as Exhibit G in the Report but not attached thereto; obtained from the Debtor\'s banking records.
72	
73	4\. **Broker Services Agreement** between Meridian Consumer Products, Inc. and Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc., dated March 1, 2022 (file: harborview-broker-agreement.docx) --- obtained from the Debtor\'s contract files.
74	
75	5\. **Engagement Letter** between Meridian Consumer Products, Inc. and Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC, dated January 8, 2025 (file: glenbrook-engagement-letter.docx) --- for reference regarding the scope and limitations of Glenbrook\'s engagement.
76	
77	Please note that the Debtor\'s pre-petition auditor is Thornfield & Associates, P.C. Additional financial records may be requested from the Debtor as needed.
78	
79	**[5. Deliverable and Format]{.underline}**
80	
81	You are to prepare a comprehensive Issues Memorandum (the \"Memorandum\") identifying all errors, omissions, analytical flaws, and legal misapplications in the Report. The Memorandum should be organized by category: (1) arithmetic and reconciliation errors, (2) entity and classification errors, (3) legal analysis errors, and (4) omissions.
82	
83	For each issue identified, the Memorandum must:
84	
85	> \(a\) describe the specific error or omission;
86	>
87	> \(b\) explain the legal or practical significance of the issue;
88	>
89	> \(c\) quantify the dollar impact where possible;
90	>
91	> \(d\) provide a corrected calculation where applicable; and
92	>
93	> \(e\) recommend specific next steps (e.g., request additional data, correct the calculation, conduct further legal research, prepare demand letter).
94	
95	The Memorandum should include a prioritization of issues by materiality and urgency, as well as a corrected preference exposure estimate where the data permits.
96	
97	The Memorandum must be suitable for review by the undersigned and for potential use in discussions with the Debtor\'s counsel (Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP) and the Debtor\'s financial advisor (Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC) regarding the adequacy of the Report. The Memorandum may also be shared with the Committee\'s financial advisor, Pinehurst Capital Advisors LLC, for their independent analysis.
98	
99	**[6. Timeline and Deadline]{.underline}**
100	
101	An initial draft of the Memorandum is due to me by **Monday, May 19, 2025** --- approximately two weeks from the date of this letter. A status call to discuss your preliminary findings is scheduled for **Monday, May 12, 2025, at 2:00 p.m. ET**. Please be prepared to discuss any threshold issues or additional document requests at that time.
102	
103	As you are aware, the statutory deadline for commencing preference actions under 11 U.S.C. § 546(a)(1) is two years from the date of the order for relief --- here, March 14, 2027. While there is no immediate time pressure, the Committee wishes to address the Report\'s adequacy promptly in order to plan its litigation strategy and potential settlement negotiations. Please also note that the Committee\'s next scheduled meeting is May 22, 2025, and the Memorandum may be discussed at that meeting.
104	
105	**[7. Coordination and Confidentiality]{.underline}**
106	
107	Please coordinate with Pinehurst Capital Advisors LLC regarding any quantitative analyses or requests for additional financial data from the Debtor. All work product in connection with this assignment is subject to attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. The Memorandum should be marked **\"PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT\"** on each page.
108	
109	Do not share the Memorandum or its contents with the Debtor, the Debtor\'s counsel, or Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC without my prior written approval. Any communications with the Debtor\'s counsel regarding the Report\'s adequacy should be directed through me.
110	
111	**[8. Closing]{.underline}**
112	
113	Daniel, I am confident in your ability to handle this assignment thoroughly and efficiently. This is a critical workstream for the Committee, and the quality of our analysis will directly inform the Committee\'s strategy regarding what may prove to be a significant source of recovery for the estate\'s unsecured creditors. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me with any questions or if you require additional resources.
114	
115	Very truly yours,

(\"Meridian\" or the \"Company\"), a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, as financial advisor in connection with the Company\'s evaluation of strategic alternatives, including a potential restructuring or reorganization under Chapter 11 of Title 11 of the United States Code (the \"Bankruptcy Code\"). 146	
147	As of the date hereof, the Company\'s approximate funded debt obligations consist of (i) a \$95 million first lien term loan facility (the \"First Lien Facility\") with Ridgeline Capital Partners, LLC, as administrative agent, and (ii) \$47 million in aggregate principal amount of 9.5% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2027 (the \"Senior Notes\") issued pursuant to an indenture with Cornerstone Trust Company, as indenture trustee. 154	
155	Glenbrook shall assist the Company\'s management in evaluating the Company\'s current liquidity position, cash flow forecasts, and available strategic alternatives. Such services shall include assisting in the preparation and review of financial projections and operating budgets, advising on restructuring alternatives including out-of-court workouts, forbearance negotiations with the Company\'s lenders, and in-court proceedings under the Bankruptcy Code, and providing such other general financial advisory services as the Company and Glenbrook may agree upon from time to time.
156	
157	**3.2 Chapter 11 Advisory Services (Contingent on Filing)**
158	
159	In the event the Company commences a voluntary case under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code (a \"Chapter 11 Filing\"), Glenbrook shall provide the following financial advisory services in support of the Company\'s restructuring process:
160	
161	> \(a\) Assisting the Company in the preparation of schedules of assets and liabilities and statements of financial affairs required under the Bankruptcy Code and the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure;
162	>
163	> \(b\) Cash management analysis and support in connection with debtor-in-possession (\"DIP\") financing, including assistance in the preparation of cash flow projections and budget-to-actual variance reporting;
164	>
165	> \(c\) Preparation of a preference exposure analysis under 11 U.S.C. § 547 (the \"Preference Exposure Report\"), which shall include: (i) identification and categorization of potential preferential transfers made during the 90-day period preceding the petition date (and the one-year period preceding the petition date for transfers to insiders, as defined in 11 U.S.C. § 101(31)); (ii) categorization of identified transfers by size tier and payee type; (iii) a preliminary assessment of potentially available statutory defenses under 11 U.S.C. § 547(c), including the ordinary course of business defense, the contemporaneous exchange defense, and the subsequent new value defense; and (iv) an estimated aggregate net preference exposure, net of identified preliminary defenses. The Preference Exposure Report shall be prepared for the informational use of the Company and its legal counsel and shall not constitute a legal opinion or definitive legal conclusion regarding the avoidability of any identified transfer;

All legal conclusions regarding the avoidability of transfers, the applicability of statutory defenses under the Bankruptcy Code, or the interpretation or application of the Bankruptcy Code or other applicable law shall be the exclusive province of the Company\'s legal counsel, Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP, or such other counsel as the Company may engage.
180	
181	Glenbrook\'s analyses and deliverables, including the Preference Exposure Report, will be based upon information provided by the Company, its management, its counsel, and its other advisors, and shall not constitute an audit or independent verification of such information. Glenbrook shall be entitled to rely upon the accuracy and completeness of all data provided by the Company, including but not limited to general ledger data, bank statements, accounts payable records, payroll records, and vendor contracts, without independent verification. Mr. Gao will be supported by a Senior Vice President and an Associate, with additional staffing allocated as the scope of the engagement requires. Glenbrook may adjust its staffing from time to time as it deems appropriate, with reasonable notice to the Company.
186	
187	The Company\'s primary point of contact for this engagement shall be Rebecca Liu-Whitford, Chief Financial Officer, and such other personnel as the Company may designate in writing to Glenbrook from time to time. The Company shall ensure that its designated contacts are authorized to provide information and direction to Glenbrook in connection with the performance of the Services.
188	
189	**[5. Fees and Expenses]{.underline}**
190	
191	**5.1 Monthly Advisory Fee**
192	
193	The Company shall pay Glenbrook a monthly advisory fee of \$125,000 (the \"Monthly Advisory Fee\"), payable in advance on the first business day of each calendar month during the term of this engagement, commencing January 2025. The Monthly Advisory Fee shall be deemed fully earned when due and shall be non-refundable once paid. In the event the engagement commences or terminates on a date other than the first or last day of a calendar month, the Monthly Advisory Fee for such partial month shall be prorated on a daily basis.
194	
195	**5.2 Completion Fee**
196	
197	In addition to the Monthly Advisory Fees, the Company shall pay Glenbrook a completion fee of \$500,000 (the \"Completion Fee\"), payable upon the earliest to occur of (a) the confirmation of a plan of reorganization under 11 U.S.C. § 1129, (b) the consummation of a sale of substantially all of the Company\'s assets under 11 U.S.C. § 363, or (c) such other milestone or event as the parties may agree in writing. The Completion Fee is in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Monthly Advisory Fees. For the avoidance of doubt, Monthly Advisory Fees previously paid shall not be credited against or deducted from the Completion Fee; the two fee components run independently of one another.
198	
199	**5.3 Hourly Rates for Litigation Support**
200	
201	If the Company requests litigation support or expert testimony services pursuant to Section 3.3, such services shall be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
202	
203	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
204	  **Title**                           **Hourly Rate**
205	  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
206	  Managing Director                   \$850
207	
208	  Senior Vice President               \$725
209	
210	  Vice President                      \$575
211	
212	  Associate                           \$425
213	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
214	
215	The foregoing hourly rates are subject to annual adjustment by Glenbrook upon 30 days\' written notice to the Company.
216	
217	**5.4 Expense Reimbursement**
218	
219	The Company shall reimburse Glenbrook for all reasonable and documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of the Services, including but not limited to travel, lodging, data processing, third-party research, and reproduction costs. Glenbrook shall obtain the Company\'s prior written approval for any single expense item exceeding \$5,000. Expense reimbursement requests shall be submitted monthly in arrears with supporting documentation.
220	
221	**5.5 Bankruptcy Court Approval**
222	
223	In the event of a Chapter 11 Filing, Glenbrook\'s retention and compensation under this Engagement Letter shall be subject to approval by the United States Bankruptcy Court having jurisdiction over the Company\'s Chapter 11 case (the \"Bankruptcy Court\") pursuant to Sections 327 and 330 of the Bankruptcy Code. Glenbrook agrees to file appropriate applications for retention and compensation, to cooperate with the Office of the United States Trustee, and to provide such information as may be required by the Bankruptcy Court and applicable guidelines.
224	
225	**[6. Information and Access]{.underline}**
226	
227	The Company agrees to provide Glenbrook with timely access to all books, records, data, and personnel reasonably necessary for the performance of the Services. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Company shall make available to Glenbrook the following categories of information and records:
228	
229	> \(a\) general ledger and sub-ledger data;
230	>
231	> \(b\) accounts payable and accounts receivable records;
232	>
233	> \(c\) bank statements and wire transfer records;
234	>
235	> \(d\) payroll and compensation records;
236	>
237	> \(e\) material contracts with vendors, customers, and lenders;
238	>
239	> \(f\) insurance policies and broker agreements;
240	>
241	> \(g\) historical financial statements, both audited and unaudited; and
242	>
243	> \(h\) such other information as Glenbrook may reasonably request from time to time.
244	
245	The Company represents and warrants that the information provided to Glenbrook in connection with this engagement will be accurate and complete in all material respects. Glenbrook shall have no obligation to independently verify or audit any information provided by the Company and shall be entitled to rely upon all such information in the performance of the Services and the preparation of its deliverables.
246	
247	**[7. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
248	
249	Glenbrook agrees to treat all non-public information received from the Company or its representatives in connection with this engagement as confidential (\"Confidential Information\") and to use such Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing the Services contemplated by this Engagement Letter. Glenbrook shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party, except as follows:
250	
251	> \(a\) information that becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this provision by Glenbrook;
252	>
253	> \(b\) information that was independently developed by Glenbrook without use of or reference to the Company\'s Confidential Information;
254	>
255	> \(c\) disclosures required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or order of the Bankruptcy Court; and
256	>
257	> \(d\) disclosures to Glenbrook\'s own legal counsel in connection with the enforcement or interpretation of this Engagement Letter.
258	
259	Notwithstanding the foregoing, Glenbrook\'s work product and deliverables may be shared with the Company\'s legal counsel, Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP, the Company\'s Board of Directors, and, in the event of a Chapter 11 Filing, with any official committee appointed in the Chapter 11 case and such committee\'s retained advisors, in each case as required by the Bankruptcy Code, the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, and applicable orders of the Bankruptcy Court.
260	
261	**[8. Indemnification]{.underline}**
262	
263	The Company agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Glenbrook, its members, managers, officers, employees, and agents (collectively, the \"Indemnified Parties\") from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses of litigation) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising out of or related to the engagement contemplated by this Engagement Letter or the performance or non-performance of the Services, except to the extent that such Losses are finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to have resulted from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of the Indemnified Parties. The Company shall advance to the Indemnified Parties any expenses incurred in defending any claim, action, or proceeding subject to this indemnification provision, pending final adjudication thereof. If the Company is unable to satisfy its indemnification obligations in full, the Company and the Indemnified Parties shall contribute to the aggregate Losses in proportion to their relative fault. The indemnification and contribution obligations set forth in this Section 8 shall survive termination of this Engagement Letter and, in the event of a Chapter 11 Filing, shall be entitled to administrative expense priority under Section 503(b) of the Bankruptcy Code.
264	
265	**[9. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**
266	
267	Glenbrook\'s aggregate liability to the Company arising out of or related to this engagement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total fees actually paid by the Company to Glenbrook under this Engagement Letter. In no event shall Glenbrook be liable to the Company or any other person for any consequential, indirect, incidental, special, or punitive damages of any nature, regardless of whether Glenbrook has been advised of the possibility of such damages. Glenbrook\'s deliverables, including the Preference Exposure Report and all other work product prepared in connection with this engagement, are prepared solely for the informational use of the Company and its counsel and are not intended to be relied upon by any third party. Glenbrook assumes no duty or liability to any third party in connection with its Services or work product delivered hereunder.
268	
269	**[10. Term and Termination]{.underline}**
270	
271	This engagement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue until the earliest to occur of (a) completion of the Services, (b) mutual written agreement of the parties to terminate the engagement, or (c) 30 calendar days following written notice of termination delivered by either party to the other. In the event of a Chapter 11 Filing, any termination of Glenbrook\'s engagement shall also be subject to applicable orders of the Bankruptcy Court. Upon termination of this engagement for any reason, the Company shall pay all accrued and unpaid Monthly Advisory Fees, the Completion Fee (if the conditions for payment thereof have been satisfied as of the date of termination), and all unreimbursed expenses through the date of termination. The provisions of Sections 7, 8, 9, and 14 shall survive termination of this Engagement Letter.
272	
273	**[11. Independent Contractor Status]{.underline}**
274	
275	Glenbrook is an independent contractor and is not an employee, agent, or fiduciary of the Company. Nothing in this Engagement Letter shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship between Glenbrook and the Company. Glenbrook\'s advice and recommendations are advisory in nature only, and all decisions regarding the Company\'s business, operations, financial affairs, and restructuring strategy remain solely with the Company\'s Board of Directors and management.
276	
277	**[12. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**
278	
279	Glenbrook represents that, as of the date hereof, it has conducted a reasonable conflicts check and is not aware of any material conflict of interest that would prevent it from performing the Services described herein. Glenbrook agrees to promptly notify the Company in writing if any potential conflict of interest arises during the term of this engagement. Glenbrook may have provided, and may in the future provide, services to creditors, vendors, or other parties-in-interest of the Company in the ordinary course of Glenbrook\'s business, and such prior or future engagements shall not constitute a conflict of interest absent a direct adverse interest to the Company in connection with this engagement. Glenbrook confirms that it has not previously provided services to Ridgeline Capital Partners, LLC, Cornerstone Trust Company, or any member of any official committee that may be appointed in a Chapter 11 case involving the Company.
280	
281	**[13. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
282	
283	This Engagement Letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof. Any dispute arising under or relating to this Engagement Letter shall be resolved by binding arbitration in New York, New York, administered under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association; *provided, however*, that in the event of a Chapter 11 Filing, the Bankruptcy Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any and all disputes relating to Glenbrook\'s retention and compensation under Sections 327 and 330 of the Bankruptcy Code.
284	
285	**[14. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**
286	
287	**Entire Agreement.** This Engagement Letter constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, understandings, or agreements, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter.
288	
289	**Amendments.** No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Engagement Letter shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by both parties.
290	
291	**Assignment.** Neither party may assign this Engagement Letter or any rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, and any purported assignment in violation of this provision shall be null and void.
292	
293	**Notices.** All notices, requests, and other communications under this Engagement Letter shall be in writing and shall be delivered to the following addresses (or such other addresses as a party may designate in writing):
294	
295	> If to Glenbrook: Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC 200 Park Avenue, 22nd Floor New York, NY 10166
296	>
297	> Attn: Jonathan Gao, Managing Director
298	>
299	> If to the Company: Meridian Consumer Products, Inc. 4200 Southpark Drive, Suite 800 Charlotte, NC 28217
300	>
301	> Attn: Rebecca Liu-Whitford, Chief Financial Officer
302	>
303	> With a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to: Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP (Debtor\'s Bankruptcy Counsel)
304	
305	**Counterparts.** This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
306	
307	**Severability.** If any provision of this Engagement Letter is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision hereof, and this Engagement Letter shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been contained herein.
308	
309	We look forward to working with you and the Company during this important engagement. Please confirm your agreement to the foregoing terms by executing and returning a copy of this letter.
310

**[BROKER SERVICES AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**March 1, 2022**

This Broker Services Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of March 1, 2022 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between **Meridian Consumer Products, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 4200 Southpark Drive, Suite 800, Charlotte, NC 28217 (\"Client\" or \"Insured\"), and **Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc.**, a Connecticut corporation, with its principal place of business at 127 Asylum Street, Suite 1400, Hartford, CT 06103 (\"Broker\"). Client and Broker are each referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Client is engaged in the manufacture and distribution of household cleaning products and personal care items and requires comprehensive commercial insurance coverage to protect its business operations, assets, employees, and third-party exposures;

**WHEREAS**, Broker is a licensed insurance broker in the State of Connecticut and is authorized to place insurance coverage with admitted and surplus lines carriers in multiple jurisdictions throughout the United States;

**WHEREAS**, Client desires to engage Broker to act as its insurance broker of record for the placement, renewal, and ongoing management of Client\'s commercial insurance program, and Broker desires to accept such engagement on the terms and conditions set forth herein;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties wish to set forth the terms and conditions governing Broker\'s brokerage services, the handling and remittance of premium payments, the compensation payable to Broker, and the respective rights and obligations of the Parties in connection therewith;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below:

**\"Carriers\"** means the insurance companies with which Broker places coverage on Client\'s behalf, including but not limited to those listed on Schedule A attached hereto. The term \"Carrier\" shall refer to any one of them individually.

**\"Commission\"** means the compensation paid to Broker by the Carriers or Client for the placement and servicing of insurance policies under the Insurance Program, whether in the form of commissions, overrides, contingent commissions, or other remuneration from Carriers.

**\"Effective Date\"** means March 1, 2022, the date on which this Agreement becomes effective.

**\"Insurance Program\"** means the comprehensive commercial insurance program maintained by Client, including general liability, product liability, property (all risk), workers\' compensation, commercial automobile, umbrella/excess liability, directors and officers liability, and such other coverages as may be added from time to time, as set forth in Schedule A attached hereto.

**\"Net Premiums\"** means the aggregate premiums payable by Client to Carriers for the Insurance Program, exclusive of Broker\'s commissions, Service Fees, and any applicable surplus lines taxes or filing fees that are separately itemized.

**\"Policy Period\"** means each annual period commencing on the anniversary of the Effective Date, or such other period as may be specified in an individual insurance policy within the Insurance Program.

**\"Premium Trust Account\"** means the segregated fiduciary account maintained by Broker at a federally insured depository institution for the deposit and remittance of Net Premiums collected from Client, as more particularly described in Section 4.3 of this Agreement.

**\"Service Fees\"** means the fees payable by Client to Broker for brokerage services rendered under this Agreement, as set forth in Section 5.1.

**[ARTICLE II --- APPOINTMENT AND SCOPE OF SERVICES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Appointment**

Client hereby appoints Broker as its exclusive insurance broker of record for the Insurance Program, effective as of the Effective Date. Broker accepts the appointment and agrees to act in the best interests of Client in the placement, management, and servicing of coverage under the Insurance Program for the duration of this Agreement.

**Section 2.2 --- Scope of Services**

Broker shall provide the following services in connection with the Insurance Program:

> \(a\) Evaluate Client\'s insurance needs and risk profile on an annual basis, taking into account changes in Client\'s operations, revenues, exposures, and industry conditions;
>
> \(b\) Obtain competitive quotations from Carriers for each line of coverage within the Insurance Program;
>
> \(c\) Negotiate policy terms, conditions, endorsements, and premiums with Carriers on Client\'s behalf;
>
> \(d\) Place coverage with Carriers selected by Client upon Broker\'s recommendation;
>
> \(e\) Manage policy renewals, endorsements, and cancellations, ensuring continuity of coverage throughout each Policy Period;
>
> \(f\) Assist Client in the submission and processing of claims, including coordination with Carriers and their adjusters;
>
> \(g\) Provide certificates of insurance to Client\'s customers, vendors, landlords, and other third parties as reasonably requested by Client;
>
> \(h\) Maintain records of all policies, endorsements, binders, and premium payments associated with the Insurance Program; and
>
> \(i\) Advise Client of material changes in the insurance market, including developments in carrier capacity, pricing trends, and regulatory changes, that may affect coverage availability or pricing under the Insurance Program.

**Section 2.3 --- Broker\'s Standard of Care**

Broker shall perform its services under this Agreement with the degree of care, skill, and diligence customarily exercised by experienced insurance brokers in the State of Connecticut handling accounts of similar size and complexity. Broker shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing insurance brokerage activities.

**[ARTICLE III --- CLIENT OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Disclosure of Information**

Client shall provide Broker with accurate and complete information regarding its business operations, risk exposures, loss history, claim activity, property valuations, and other matters relevant to the placement and maintenance of the Insurance Program. Client shall promptly notify Broker of any material changes in its operations, financial condition, or risk profile that may affect existing or prospective coverage.

**Section 3.2 --- Cooperation**

Client shall cooperate with Broker in completing insurance applications, providing underwriting information requested by Carriers, and responding to carrier inquiries in a timely manner so as not to impair or delay the placement or renewal of coverage.

**Section 3.3 --- Premium Payment Obligations**

Client shall pay all premiums and fees as set forth in Articles IV and V of this Agreement. Client acknowledges that failure to timely pay premiums may result in cancellation or non-renewal of coverage by the applicable Carrier, and that Broker shall not be liable for any lapse in coverage resulting from Client\'s failure to make timely premium payments.

**[ARTICLE IV --- PREMIUM COLLECTION AND REMITTANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Premium Billing**

Broker shall invoice Client for all Net Premiums due to Carriers and for all Service Fees due to Broker. Invoices shall be issued not less than thirty (30) days prior to the applicable premium due date established by each Carrier. Each invoice shall separately itemize: (a) Net Premiums payable to each Carrier, identified by line of coverage and policy number; and (b) Service Fees payable to Broker under Section 5.1.

**Section 4.2 --- Payment Terms**

Client shall remit payment of all invoiced amounts within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Payments of Net Premiums shall be made by wire transfer or check payable to \"Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc. --- Premium Trust Account.\" Payments of Service Fees shall be made by wire transfer or check payable to \"Harborview Insurance Brokers, Inc.\" Client may remit Net Premiums and Service Fees in a single payment, provided that Broker shall allocate such payment in accordance with the provisions of this Article IV.

**Section 4.3 --- Segregated Premium Trust Account**

All Net Premiums received by Broker from Client shall be held by Broker in a fiduciary capacity for the benefit of the applicable Carriers. Broker shall deposit all Net Premiums received from Client into a segregated premium trust account (the \"Premium Trust Account\") maintained at a federally insured depository institution, separate and apart from Broker\'s general operating funds.

Funds held in the Premium Trust Account shall at all times remain the property of the applicable Carriers (or, to the extent not yet remitted, shall be held in trust for such Carriers) and shall not constitute property of Broker or of Client. Broker shall remit Net Premiums from the Premium Trust Account to the applicable Carriers within fifteen (15) business days of receipt from Client, or such earlier date as may be required by the applicable Carrier or by law.

Broker shall not commingle funds in the Premium Trust Account with Broker\'s own funds or with any other funds not held in a fiduciary capacity. Broker shall maintain the Premium Trust Account in accordance with the requirements of the Connecticut Insurance Code and all other applicable statutes, regulations, and rules governing fiduciary accounts maintained by insurance brokers.

In the event of any insolvency, bankruptcy, or receivership proceeding involving Client or Broker, the Parties acknowledge and agree that funds held in the Premium Trust Account are trust funds held in a fiduciary capacity and are not property of the estate of either Client or Broker. The obligations of Broker under this Section 4.3 are fiduciary in nature and shall not be discharged, modified, or affected by any bankruptcy, insolvency, or similar proceeding.

**Section 4.4 --- Broker\'s Remittance Obligations**

Broker shall remit to each Carrier the Net Premiums due to such Carrier in accordance with the payment terms established between Broker and such Carrier. Broker shall provide Client with written confirmation of each remittance within five (5) business days of payment to the applicable Carrier. Broker shall maintain complete and accurate records of all premium receipts from Client and all remittances to Carriers and shall make such records available to Client upon reasonable request.

**Section 4.5 --- Allocation of Payments**

In the event that Client makes a lump-sum payment covering both Net Premiums and Service Fees, Broker shall first allocate the payment to Net Premiums (depositing such amounts into the Premium Trust Account) and shall allocate the remainder to Service Fees. This allocation priority shall apply regardless of any payment instructions or designations to the contrary provided by Client.

**[ARTICLE V --- COMPENSATION]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Service Fees**

As compensation for the services described in Section 2.2, Client shall pay Broker an annual Service Fee of Five Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$520,000), payable in quarterly installments of One Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$130,000) each, due on the first business day of each calendar quarter during the term of this Agreement. Service Fees are earned by Broker upon receipt and are not held in a fiduciary capacity. Service Fees shall be deposited into Broker\'s general operating account and shall not be deposited into the Premium Trust Account.

**Section 5.2 --- Carrier Commissions**

In addition to Service Fees, Broker may receive commissions from Carriers in connection with the placement, renewal, and servicing of coverage under the Insurance Program. Broker shall disclose to Client the amount and source of all commissions received from Carriers on an annual basis. Carrier commissions shall not reduce or offset the Service Fees payable by Client under Section 5.1.

**Section 5.3 --- Expenses**

Client shall reimburse Broker for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of Broker\'s services under this Agreement, including travel expenses, filing fees, and surplus lines taxes. Broker shall provide receipts and itemized statements for all expenses exceeding Five Hundred Dollars (\$500). Client shall reimburse approved expenses within thirty (30) days of receipt of an itemized expense statement.

**[ARTICLE VI --- INSURANCE PROGRAM AND CARRIER SELECTION]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Carrier Qualifications**

Broker shall place coverage under the Insurance Program only with Carriers that maintain a financial strength rating of \"A-\" (Excellent) or better as rated by A.M. Best Company or another nationally recognized insurance rating agency, unless Client provides prior written consent to placement with a Carrier rated below that threshold.

**Section 6.2 --- Current Insurance Program**

The current Insurance Program, including the Carriers, policy numbers, and estimated annual Net Premiums for each line of coverage, is set forth in **Schedule A** attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. Broker shall update Schedule A on each anniversary of the Effective Date to reflect current coverage, Carriers, policy numbers, and premium amounts.

**Section 6.3 --- Changes to Coverage**

Broker shall not materially modify, cancel, or non-renew any coverage under the Insurance Program without Client\'s prior written consent. Broker shall promptly notify Client of any Carrier\'s intent to cancel, non-renew, or materially alter the terms or conditions of any coverage.

**[ARTICLE VII --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Initial Term**

This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for an initial term of three (3) years, expiring on February 28, 2025, unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article VII.

**Section 7.2 --- Renewal**

Upon expiration of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1)-year periods unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. Each renewal term shall be subject to the same terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, unless the Parties agree in writing to modify such terms.

**Section 7.3 --- Termination for Cause**

Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice to the other Party if the other Party: (a) materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within such thirty (30)-day notice period; or (b) becomes the subject of a voluntary or involuntary petition in bankruptcy, makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or is placed in receivership or liquidation proceedings.

**Section 7.4 --- Effect of Termination**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason:

> \(a\) Broker shall remit all Net Premiums then held in the Premium Trust Account to the applicable Carriers within ten (10) business days of the effective date of termination;
>
> \(b\) Broker shall transfer Client\'s insurance files, records, policy documents, and related materials to Client or to Client\'s successor broker within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination;
>
> \(c\) Client shall pay all outstanding Service Fees and reimbursable expenses incurred through the effective date of termination within thirty (30) days of receipt of Broker\'s final invoice; and
>
> \(d\) The fiduciary obligations set forth in Section 4.3 shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement with respect to any funds remaining in the Premium Trust Account until all such funds have been remitted to the applicable Carriers.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- RECORDS, REPORTING, AND AUDIT RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Recordkeeping**

Broker shall maintain accurate and complete records of all transactions related to the Insurance Program, including premium receipts from Client, remittances to Carriers, commissions received, claims submissions, and correspondence with Carriers. Broker shall retain such records for a period of not less than seven (7) years following the expiration of the applicable Policy Period.

**Section 8.2 --- Reporting**

Broker shall provide Client with quarterly reports, delivered within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter, detailing: (a) premiums received from Client during the quarter; (b) premiums remitted to each Carrier during the quarter; (c) the current balance in the Premium Trust Account; and (d) a summary of claims activity under the Insurance Program.

**Section 8.3 --- Audit Rights**

Client shall have the right, upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior written notice to Broker, to audit or examine Broker\'s books, records, and accounts relating to the Insurance Program and the Premium Trust Account. Broker shall cooperate fully with any such audit and shall provide reasonable access to its personnel and facilities.

**[ARTICLE IX --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Broker Representations**

Broker represents and warrants to Client that:

> \(a\) Broker is duly licensed as an insurance broker in the State of Connecticut and in all other jurisdictions in which it places coverage on Client\'s behalf, and all such licenses are in good standing;
>
> \(b\) Broker has the corporate authority and legal capacity to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
>
> \(c\) The Premium Trust Account is and shall at all times during the term of this Agreement be maintained in compliance with the Connecticut Insurance Code, including without limitation the provisions thereof governing fiduciary accounts maintained by insurance brokers, and all other applicable laws, regulations, and rules; and
>
> \(d\) Broker will comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations in the performance of its services under this Agreement.

**Section 9.2 --- Client Representations**

Client represents and warrants to Broker that:

> \(a\) Client is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware;
>
> \(b\) Client has the corporate authority and legal capacity to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder; and
>
> \(c\) The information provided to Broker regarding Client\'s business operations, risk exposures, loss history, and financial condition is accurate and complete in all material respects as of the Effective Date.

**[ARTICLE X --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Client Indemnification**

Client shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Broker and its officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, judgments, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or related to: (a) Client\'s failure to provide accurate or complete information to Broker; (b) Client\'s failure to timely pay premiums resulting in cancellation or non-renewal of coverage; or (c) Client\'s material breach of this Agreement.

**Section 10.2 --- Broker Indemnification**

Broker shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Client and its officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, judgments, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or related to: (a) Broker\'s negligent acts or omissions in the performance of its services under this Agreement; (b) Broker\'s failure to remit Net Premiums to Carriers resulting in cancellation or non-renewal of coverage; (c) Broker\'s misappropriation or commingling of funds in the Premium Trust Account; or (d) Broker\'s material breach of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE XI --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

 ["TO:", "Margaret R. Shelton, Partner"],
 ["FROM:", "Daniel Voss, Senior Associate"],
 ["DATE:", "May 19, 2025 (initial draft)"],
 ["RE:", "Issues Memorandum \u2014 Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC Preference Exposure Report dated April 30, 2025; In re Meridian Consumer Products, Inc., Case No. 25-10347-KWH (Bankr. D. Del.) (Hensley, J.)"],
 ["CLIENT:", "Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors of Meridian Consumer Products, Inc."],
], widths=[1.0, 5.5], size=10)
P("**Distribution restriction:** Per your May 5, 2025 instructions, this Memorandum is not to be shared with the Debtor, Westbrook, Hale & Jennings LLP, or Glenbrook Advisory Group LLC without your prior written approval. It may be shared with Pinehurst Capital Advisors LLC for its independent analysis.", italic=False, size=9, align="j")

H("I. Executive Summary", 1)
P("I reviewed the Glenbrook Preference Exposure Report dated April 30, 2025 (the \u201cReport\u201d) against the five supporting records provided with the assignment: the payroll and insider compensation records (the Report’s unattached Exhibit F), the Consolidated Plastics wire transfer records (the Report’s unattached Exhibit G), the Harborview Broker Services Agreement dated March 1, 2022, the Glenbrook engagement letter dated January 8, 2025, and your assignment letter. The Report cannot be relied on in its current form. Its headline figures do not reconcile to its own exhibits. It names the wrong transferee for one Tier 1 payee. It states that there were no insider transfers when the Debtor’s own records show $1,048,000 of them. It gets the statute of limitations and the § 547(c)(9) threshold wrong. And it credits $8.23 million of defenses, most of which are unsupported or legally misapplied, all in the defendants’ favor.", align="j")
P("**Key findings:**", space_after=2)
B("**The numbers do not reconcile.** The 81 payees listed in Exhibit A total **$24,115,581**, not the $18,732,614 headline, a gap of $5,382,967. Every tier subtotal is wrong. Tier 1 is said to have 6 payees, but only 3 are named. Exhibit A lists 81 payees, not 84. The detailed schedules for Vanderhoff ($6,979,000 vs. $6,800,000 stated) and TerraFreight ($2,567,000 vs. $2,900,000 stated) do not add up to the totals the Report states. The Report gives two different net exposure figures: $11.2 million in the Executive Summary and $10,502,614 in Section V.E.")
B("**Tiers are misclassified.** Four payees above the $500,000 Tier 1 threshold are placed in Tier 2: Sagebrush ($1.8M), Harborview ($1.5M), Consolidated Plastics ($1.4M) and DataStream ($1.2M). The Report’s demand letter recommendation therefore leaves out four of the seven largest targets.")
B("**Wrong transferee.** Every Consolidated Plastics wire went to **CPI Americas, Inc. (Delaware)**, not to the Hong Kong entity named in the Report. The bank records show 12 wires, not 7, and none of them matches Exhibit C by date, amount or reference number. The wires came from a First Hollcroft Bank of Charlotte account (****4738), which is not one of the three bank accounts the Report says it reviewed.")
B("**$1,048,000 in insider transfers was omitted.** These are Hutchins’s severance ($525,000) and consulting fee ($175,000), the CFO’s retention bonus ($300,000), and Thibodeau’s above-market commissions ($48,000). The Report says \u201cno insider transfers were identified.\u201d The CFO who received the $300,000 bonus is also Glenbrook’s designated client contact and approved every CPI wire. That is a material independence problem.")
B("**Defenses are misapplied.** (i) The earmarking credit of $750,000 has no legal basis. (ii) Four \u201ccontemporaneous exchange\u201d transfers paid 8\u201314 days after delivery ($485,000) do not qualify, and the remaining § 547(c)(1) amounts exceed the payees’ entire aggregate transfers. (iii) The Vanderhoff new value credit is overstated: the Exhibit E credits total $3.1M, not $3.2M, and $345,000 of December new value was credited to payments it cannot offset. (iv) The ordinary course credits ($2.94M) rest on a pre-2005 conjunctive standard, and the Report did no debtor-creditor (subjective) analysis.")
B("**Harborview needs a different analysis.** Under the Broker Services Agreement, net premiums are deposited in a segregated Premium Trust Account and held for the carriers. Harborview’s exposure is likely limited to its own service fees ($130,000 per quarter). The premium portion should be analyzed against the carriers as initial transferees, and they have strong defenses.")
B("**Statutory errors.** The § 546(a)(1) deadline is two years after the order for relief, not one year. Here that is **March 15, 2027**, because March 14, 2027 is a Sunday (Fed. R. Bankr. P. 9006(a)(1)(C)). The Report says March 14, 2026. The § 547(c)(9) threshold for this case is **$7,575**, not $5,000. That removes 17 more payees ($101,281).")
P("**Corrected exposure.** Using the payee-level detail and only the defenses the documents support, I estimate corrected gross exposure of about **$23.54 million** and net exposure of about **$20.11 million**, compared with the Report’s $10.50 million (or $11.2 million). Even starting from the Report’s unreconciled $18.73 million headline, the same adjustments produce net exposure of about **$14.73 million**. If TerraFreight and DataStream ultimately prove ordinary course defenses in the amounts Glenbrook asserted, net exposure falls to about $17.17 million. Section VIII sets out the build-up and sensitivities. Every figure here is preliminary until the Debtor produces transfer-level ledger and bank data.", align="j")
P("**Immediate priorities (before the May 22, 2025 Committee meeting):** (1) a written request through you to Westbrook for the full transfer-level ledger, the bank statements for all accounts (including First Hollcroft ****4738), and the complete payroll and insider records; (2) a litigation hold and preservation request covering insider and CPI records; (3) an evaluation of a Cybergenics derivative-standing motion in light of the CFO’s conflict; and (4) handing Pinehurst the reconciliation and new value recalculations for independent confirmation.", align="j")

H("II. Documents Reviewed and Approach", 1)
T(["Document", "Description / Use"], [
 ["preference-exposure-report.docx", "Glenbrook Preference Exposure Report (Apr. 30, 2025), narrative Sections I\u2013VIII and Exhibits A\u2013E; Exhibits F and G referenced but not attached. Footer marks the document \u201cDraft.\u201d"],
 ["payroll-insider-records.xlsx", "Officer compensation ledger (Mar. 2024\u2013Mar. 2025), Commission Plan Comparison, and Summary of Insider Payments (Exhibit F)."],
 ["wire-transfer-records-cpi.xlsx", "Bank wire records for all payments on the CPI account Sept. 12, 2024 \u2013 Mar. 14, 2025, compiled by Jonathan Gao of Glenbrook on Apr. 22, 2025 (Exhibit G)."],
 ["harborview-broker-agreement.docx", "Broker Services Agreement (Mar. 1, 2022), including Premium Trust Account provisions (\u00a7\u00a7 4.2\u20134.5), Service Fees (\u00a7 5.1), and Schedule A premium schedule."],
 ["glenbrook-engagement-letter.docx", "Glenbrook engagement (Jan. 8, 2025): scope (\u00a7 3.2(c), (f)), reliance limitations (\u00a7\u00a7 3.4, 6, 9), fees (\u00a7 5)."],
 ["committee-engagement-letter.docx", "Assignment letter (May 5, 2025) defining review categories (a)\u2013(i) and deliverable format."],
], widths=[2.0, 4.5], size=9)
P("I recomputed every total I could from the transfer-level and payee-level data in the Report and the supporting spreadsheets. H("III. Prioritization of Issues by Materiality and Urgency", 1)
P("Materiality reflects the estimated dollar effect on net exposure or recoverability. Urgency reflects whether action is needed before the May 22 Committee meeting, before any settlement or demand activity, or simply before litigation.", align="j")
T(["#", "Issue", "Category", "Est. $ Impact on Net Exposure", "Materiality", "Urgency"], [
 ["4.1", "Insider transfers omitted (Hutchins, Liu-Whitford, Thibodeau)", "Omission", "+$1,048,000 (plus fraudulent-transfer upside)", "High", "Immediate"],
 ["1.1", "Headline gross does not reconcile to payee detail; tier subtotals and counts wrong", "Arithmetic", "+$5,382,967 (detail basis)", "High", "Immediate"],
 ["2.2", "CPI transferee misidentified; 12 vs 7 wires; unreviewed bank account", "Entity", "Recoverability of $1,400,000; data integrity across all payees", "High", "Immediate"],
 ["3.6", "Earmarking misapplied to Lakeshore", "Legal", "+$750,000", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["3.3", "Ordinary course defense misstated and unsupported (TerraFreight, DataStream)", "Legal", "+$2,940,000 (credits withdrawn pending analysis)", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["3.5 / 1.5", "Vanderhoff new value overstated; Exhibit E arithmetic", "Legal / Arithmetic", "+$624,000 to +$1,024,000 net", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["3.4 / 1.7", "Contemporaneous exchange credits overstated", "Legal / Arithmetic", "+$665,000", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["3.7", "Harborview premium trust / conduit analysis absent", "Legal", "\u2212$1,370,000 against Harborview (shift to carriers)", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["2.1", "Four Tier 1 payees misclassified as Tier 2", "Classification", "Prioritization of $5,900,000", "High", "Before demands"],
 ["1.3 / 1.4", "Vanderhoff and TerraFreight schedules do not foot", "Arithmetic", "+$179,000 / \u2212$333,000", "Medium", "Before demands"],
 ["3.1", "Statute of limitations misstated (one year vs two years)", "Legal", "Timing/strategy (no $ change)", "Medium", "Calendar now"],
 ["3.2", "Outdated \u00a7 547(c)(9) threshold ($5,000 vs $7,575)", "Legal", "\u2212$101,281 (17 payees)", "Low", "Before demands"],
 ["3.8", "0% liquidation assumption and insolvency analysis unsupported", "Legal", "Element of proof for all claims; insider claims pre-9/30/24", "Medium", "Before litigation"],
 ["4.3", "Payments to lenders, noteholders, professionals not addressed", "Omission", "Unknown; potentially material", "Medium", "Data request now"],
 ["4.5", "BrightMart setoff / \u00a7 553(b) not analyzed", "Omission", "Unknown (BrightMart claim ~$4.2M)", "Medium", "Data request now"],
 ["4.7 / 3.10", "Glenbrook independence; CFO conflict; derivative standing", "Omission / Legal", "Process and credibility", "High", "Immediate"],
 ["1.6, 1.2, 1.8", "Conflicting net totals; transfer counts; non-business-day dates", "Arithmetic", "Credibility of data", "Medium", "Data request now"],
 ["4.2, 4.4, 4.6, 4.8", "Foreign enforcement, due diligence/venue, data gaps, \u00a7\u00a7 544/548", "Omission", "Varies", "Medium", "Before litigation"],

Exhibit C gives 94 detailed transfers (seven payees), plus 37 for the \u201cremaining 15 Tier 2 payees\u201d (Exhibit A shows 51 for those same payees), plus 99 for Tier 3 (Exhibit A shows 70), for 230. Footnote 2 to Exhibit A says the total includes \u201c37 transfers to Tier 3 payees not individually listed (aggregate amounts ranging from $5,001 to $4,950).\u201d That statement is incoherent: the range runs backwards, and all 59 Tier 3 payees are in fact listed."],
 ["Transfer counts drive the § 547(c)(9) analysis, ordinary course timing, and new value sequencing, and they must match the bank records for any complaint. The inconsistencies suggest that summary rows were adjusted to hit a predetermined total."],
 "Not separately quantifiable; affects the reliability of every payee total.",
 ["No reliable corrected count is possible without the transfer-level data. On Exhibit A’s line items, 215 transfers to 81 payees are documented."],
 ["Include a reconciled transfer count in the document request (Issue 1.1).",
  "Ask Glenbrook to explain Footnote 2 and the 37-transfer figure in writing."], "Medium / Data request now")

ISSUE("1.3", "Vanderhoff Exhibit C transfers total $6,979,000, not $6,800,000",
 ["The 28 Vanderhoff transfers listed in Exhibit C (VCS-001 through VCS-028), and the same 28 payments in Exhibit E, sum to **$6,979,000**. Both exhibits state a subtotal of $6,800,000."],
 ["Vanderhoff is the largest target. Understating its gross transfers by $179,000 understates the claim and carries through to the new value netting and the net exposure."],
 "+$179,000 gross (and net) exposure.",
 ["Sum of VCS-001 to VCS-028 = $6,979,000. Corrected net after properly applied new value: see Issue 3.5."],
 ["Confirm against the bank statements, especially the three transfers dated on non-business days (Issue 1.8)."], "Medium / Before demands")

ISSUE("1.4", "TerraFreight Exhibit C transfers total $2,567,000, not $2,900,000",
 ["The 19 TerraFreight transfers (TFL-001 through TFL-019) sum to **$2,567,000**. The Report uses $2,900,000 in Section IV.C, Section V.A, the V.E table and Exhibits A\u2013C. Its ordinary course split ($2,100,000 qualifying / $800,000 not qualifying) is therefore built on a base that does not exist in the detail."],
 ["Either the detail is incomplete or the payee total is overstated by $333,000. Either way, the $2.1M ordinary course credit cannot be tied to particular transfers, and the transferee bears that burden under § 547(g)."],
 "\u2212$333,000 gross exposure (if the detail is correct).",
 ["Sum of TFL-001 to TFL-019 = $2,567,000. The ordinary course credit is withdrawn pending a transfer-by-transfer analysis (Issue 3.3)."],
 ["Request the TerraFreight invoices (invoice dates and amounts) for all 19 transfers and 24 months of pre-preference payment history."], "Medium / Before demands")

ISSUE("1.5", "Exhibit E new value credits total $3,100,000, not $3,200,000",
 ["The 17 new value shipments credited in Exhibit E (PO-MCP-7721 through PO-MCP-7891) sum to **$3,100,000**. The Report claims $3,200,000 in Sections IV.A and V.C, the V.E table and the Exhibit E summary. It also says the net is $6,800,000 \u2212 $3,200,000 = $3,600,000. On Exhibit E’s own figures, the net is $6,979,000 \u2212 $3,100,000 = $3,879,000, even before the sequencing errors discussed in Issue 3.5."],
 ["The defense is overstated by $100,000 on simple arithmetic alone, before any legal objection."],
 "+$100,000 net exposure from the arithmetic error alone. The total Vanderhoff correction is addressed in Issue 3.5.",
 ["$450,000 + $380,000 + $320,000 + $185,000 + $120,000 + $145,000 + $110,000 + $95,000 + $130,000 + $105,000 + $140,000 + $115,000 + $125,000 + $110,000 + $90,000 + $80,000 + $400,000 = $3,100,000."],
 ["Have Pinehurst re-run the new value ledger from Vanderhoff’s shipping and receiving records (bills of lading, receiving reports), not from POs."], "High / Before demands")

ISSUE("1.6", "Two different net exposure figures",
 ["The Executive Summary states net exposure of \u201capproximately $11.2 million.\u201d Section V.E computes $18,732,614 \u2212 $8,230,000 = **$10,502,614**. The defense total of $8,230,000 does foot ($2.1M + $0.84M + $1.34M + $3.2M + $0.75M), but the $11.2M figure does not tie to anything in the Report."],
 ["Conflicting bottom lines undermine the Report as a basis for settlement or Committee reporting, and they suggest the Executive Summary was not updated after the analysis changed."],
 "$697,386 discrepancy between the Report’s own figures. Both are superseded by Section VIII of this Memorandum.",
 ["See corrected estimate, Section VIII."],
 ["Ask Glenbrook to identify which figure is current and to provide its working papers."], "Medium / Data request now")

ISSUE("1.7", "Contemporaneous exchange amounts exceed the payees’ total preference-period transfers",
 ["For 10 of the 11 payees in Exhibit D, the amount claimed as a § 547(c)(1) exchange is larger than, or equal to, the payee’s entire aggregate preference-period transfers as shown in Exhibit A. No payee can have a defense larger than the transfers it received.",
  ("table", ["Payee", "Exh. D amount(s)", "Exh. A aggregate", "Maximum creditable"], [
   ["Brightfield Supply Co.", "$95,000", "$95,000", "$95,000"],
   ["Cascade Chemicals, Inc.", "$112,000", "$92,000", "$92,000"],
   ["Ironwood Materials Co.", "$88,000", "$88,000", "$88,000"],
   ["Pioneer Label Systems, LLC", "$125,000", "$85,000", "$85,000"],
   ["Ridgewood Supply Co.", "$78,000", "$487,000", "$78,000"],
   ["Hawthorne Freight Services, Inc.", "$145,000", "$82,000", "$82,000"],
   ["Willow Creek Additives, LLC", "$115,000", "$78,000", "$78,000"],
   ["Summit Adhesives Co.", "$97,000 + $90,000 = $187,000", "$77,000", "$77,000"],
   ["Graystone Industrial Cleaning, LLC", "$135,000", "$72,000", "$0 (fails timing \u2014 Issue 3.4)"],
   ["Clearview Bottle Corp.", "$118,000", "$68,000", "$0 (fails timing)"],
   ["Northland Chemical Distributors, Inc.", "$142,000", "$65,000", "$0 (fails timing)"],
   ["Total", "$1,340,000", "\u2014", "$675,000"],
  ], [2.2, 1.6, 1.2, 1.5], 8, True),
  "If the Exhibit D amounts are correct, then several Tier 3 payees (for example Hawthorne at $145,000 and Summit at $187,000) actually belong in Tier 2, and gross exposure is understated."],
 ["The defense is overstated on its face, and the overlap shows that Exhibits A and D were not prepared from the same data set."],
 "At least $180,000 of the $855,000 \u201c0\u20133 day\u201d group cannot be credited ($855,000 \u2212 $675,000). Combined with Issue 3.4, net exposure rises by $665,000.",
 ["Maximum credit for the eight 0\u20133 day transfers, capped at each payee’s Exhibit A aggregate: $95,000 + $92,000 + $88,000 + $85,000 + $78,000 + $82,000 + $78,000 + $77,000 = **$675,000**."],
 ["Request invoices, delivery receipts and payment records for all 12 Exhibit D transfers.",
  "Resolve whether Exhibit A or Exhibit D carries the correct payee amounts. If Exhibit D is correct, re-tier the affected payees."], "High / Before demands")

ISSUE("1.8", "Transfers dated on non-business days; Exhibit C was not reconciled to bank records",
 ["Exhibit C states that wire dates are execution dates and check dates are bank clearing dates.  ["These dates cannot be bank clearing or execution dates. They look like ERP entry or posting dates, which contradicts the methodology stated in Section II.C. Under Barnhill v.  "Up to $805,000 of Vanderhoff gross exposure is at risk on timing, though the net Vanderhoff exposure is the same under either dating (Issue 3.5). Other amounts affected: $655,000.",
 ["Not computable without bank data. See the Vanderhoff alternative computation in Issue 3.5."],
 ["Obtain bank statements and Fedwire confirmations for every transfer dated within five days of December 14, 2024, and for all non-business-day entries.",
  "Re-date every transfer using bank clearing (checks) and settlement (wires) data."], "Medium / Data request now")

ISSUE("3.5", "Vanderhoff subsequent new value: sequencing errors and an unaddressed post-petition payment",
 ["Section V.C says each shipment was credited “against the immediately preceding preferential payment.” It then credits December 16, 18 and 20 shipments totaling **$1,150,000** against the December 14 and 15 payments, which total only **$805,000**. Under § 547(c)(4), new value can offset only preferential transfers made **before** it was given. New value in excess of the earlier unoffset preferences cannot be carried forward against later payments. The excess $345,000 is therefore lost. Separately, Exhibit E credits a $400,000 shipment on March 10, 2025 (PO-MCP-7891), the same day as a $242,000 payment, and then lists a **post-petition** $400,000 payment to Vanderhoff on March 18, 2025 (W-84920 / INV-VCS-12048) that appears to pay for that very shipment. The narrative never mentions the post-petition payment.",
  "My running-balance recomputation (all 28 Exhibit E payments, $6,979,000; new value applied only against earlier unoffset preferences) is below:",
  ("table", ["New value date", "Shipment", "Report credit", "Unoffset preferences before shipment", "Allowable credit", "Balance after"], rows, [0.8, 0.9, 1.4, 1.3, 1.0, 1.0], 8, True)],
 ["- **Sequencing:** the over-credit of $345,000 is a clear error. Under the running-balance method, every later shipment is fully usable, because unoffset payments always exceed it.",
  "- **Same-day shipment (Mar. 10):** the creditor must prove the new value was given **after** the $242,000 payment that day. Without time-stamped receiving records, the credit is open to challenge.",
  "- **Post-petition payment (Mar. 18):** under the Third Circuit’s test in New York City Shoes, Inc. v. Bentley Int’l, Inc. (In re New York City Shoes, Inc.), 880 F.2d 679 (3d Cir. 1989), new value counts if the debtor had not fully paid for it as of the petition date. Some courts, e.g., Friedman’s Liquidating Trust v. Roth Staffing Cos., 738 F.3d 547 (4th Cir. 2013), hold that post-petition payment does not reduce the defense. Delaware bankruptcy decisions are not uniform, especially where payment was made under a critical-vendor order or on a § 503(b)(9) claim. If the payment was **not** court-authorized, it is avoidable under § 549 regardless. This needs targeted research and the docket (first-day orders).",
  "- **Dating:** if the Dec. 14/15 “weekend” wires actually executed on Dec. 13 (Issue 1.8), gross falls by $805,000, and the December shipments have nothing to offset ($1,150,000 lost). Net exposure is unchanged at $4,224,000.",
  "- **Unanalyzed risk:** Vanderhoff’s 38–52 day payments on Net 45 terms, against a 42-day historical average, give it a credible ordinary course defense. Defenses cannot be stacked against the same dollars, but this is a real litigation risk the Report never mentions."],
 "Net Vanderhoff exposure rises from $3,600,000 to **$4,224,000** (+$624,000). If the Mar. 10 shipment is disallowed it rises to **$4,624,000** (+$1,024,000). If the Mar. 18 payment is avoided under § 549, the estate recovers an additional $400,000.",
 ["Gross $6,979,000 − allowable new value $2,755,000 = **$4,224,000** (base case). Alternative: $6,979,000 − $2,355,000 = $4,624,000 (Mar. 10 shipment disallowed)."],
 ["Check the docket for a critical-vendor or § 503(b)(9) order authorizing the Mar. 18 payment. If none, add a § 549 count.",
  "Obtain Vanderhoff bills of lading and receiving records with time stamps, especially for Dec. 16–20 and Mar. 10.",
  "Research Delaware treatment of post-petition-paid new value (critical-vendor context) in light of New York City Shoes.",
  "Pinehurst to rebuild the ledger from source documents and to evaluate Vanderhoff’s likely ordinary course defense."], "High / Before demands")

ISSUE("3.6", "Earmarking doctrine misapplied to the $750,000 Lakeshore payment",
 ["Glenbrook excludes the $750,000 Lakeshore wire of January 30, 2025 (LPS-007, referencing PO #MC-2024-8871) because BrightMart “directed Meridian to pay” Lakeshore and the funds were “effectively designated” for Lakeshore. The Report identifies no funds that BrightMart actually advanced, no agreement among BrightMart, the Debtor and Lakeshore, and no segregated account. The payment came out of a Debtor account (W-84570). The Report also says BrightMart “did not receive any transfers” and “owed the Debtor money” during the period. In other words, BrightMart was a customer and account debtor, not a new lender stepping in to pay an old creditor."],
 ["Earmarking is a narrow, judge-made exception. It generally applies where a third party (typically a new lender) lends funds to the debtor under an agreement that they be used to pay a specific existing creditor, the agreement is carried out, and the transaction as a whole does not diminish the estate. See, e.g., McCuskey v. Nat’l Bank of Waterloo (In re Bohlen Enters., Ltd.), 859 F.2d 561 (8th Cir. 1988). A customer’s payment of its own purchase price is a receivable of the Debtor. Once collected, those funds are property of the Debtor. A customer’s instruction about how to use them does not convert them into third-party funds, and paying Lakeshore diminished the estate dollar for dollar. If BrightMart’s payment was itself a satisfaction of BrightMart’s own obligation to the Debtor, earmarking fails outright. The $750,000 payment is also more than four times the average of Lakeshore’s other 13 payments ($180,769), which suggests a catch-up payment on antecedent debt. That makes ordinary course unlikely as well."],
 "+$750,000 net exposure.",
 ["Lakeshore net = $3,100,000 gross with no earmarking credit = **$3,100,000** (subject to any properly proven ordinary course or new value defense)."],
 ["Request PO #MC-2024-8871, all BrightMart–Meridian–Lakeshore correspondence, and Debtor bank records showing the source of the January 30, 2025 funds and any BrightMart remittance.",
  "Research Third Circuit and Delaware authority on earmarking outside the new-lender context and cite-check Bohlen.",
  "Evaluate whether BrightMart received any benefit (e.g., as guarantor or through setoff) that could support a claim against BrightMart under § 550(a)(1) as an entity for whose benefit the transfer was made."], "High / Before demands")

ISSUE("3.7", "Harborview: premium-trust funds, conduit status, and “interest of the debtor in property”",
 ["Under the Broker Services Agreement: (i) net premiums must be paid to the “Premium Trust Account” (§ 4.2); (ii) Harborview holds them “in a fiduciary capacity for the benefit of the applicable Carriers,” keeps them segregated, may not commingle them, and must remit them within 15 business days (§ 4.3); (iii) the funds “shall not constitute property of Broker or of Client” (§ 4.3); (iv) lump-sum payments are allocated first to premiums (§ 4.5); and (v) only the Service Fees of $520,000 per year ($130,000 per quarter, due on the first business day of each quarter) are Harborview’s own revenue (§ 5.1). Schedule A shows estimated annual net premiums of $980,000. Notably, $980,000 + $520,000 = $1,500,000, exactly the amount paid to Harborview in the 90-day period.
